interest: Illuminates early Nippon Hoso Kyokai administration, domestic media relations, and Japan's transition to international wartime propaganda.
overview: This file documents the development, regulation, and international projection of Japanese radio broadcasting from 1931 to 1938. The centerpiece is an exhaustive 1931 consular report detailing the legal administration, educational utilization, receiver distribution, and technical infrastructure of broadcasting under Nippon Hoso Kyokai. Subsequent records address domestic radio-press non-competition agreements, mutual Sino-Japanese short-wave propaganda following the 1937 Marco Polo Bridge incident, and Tokyo's 1938 short-wave cultural goodwill broadcasts directed to Brazil.
